lessons.title: Course Introduction: From Relational to NoSQL Thinking

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page comparison mapping the CAP theorem's three properties (consistency, availability, partition tolerance) to a real outage scenario, then list 2 concrete trade-offs BASE (vs. ACID) creates for an application you'd build on MongoDB.
slots.deliverable: A one-page CAP/BASE trade-off writeup naming a concrete scenario and 2 real application-level consequences.

lessons.title: Document, Key-Value, Column-Family & Graph Models Compared
Setting Up Your NoSQL Lab Environment

slots.practicalActivity: Pull Docker images for mongo:7, the Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator, and neo4j:5 (don't run them yet), confirm all three pulled with `docker images`, and sketch a one-page table of document vs. key-value vs. column-family vs. graph with one real example use case for each.
slots.deliverable: A `docker images` listing showing the three pulled images plus a one-page model-comparison table with a real example per model.

slots.practicalActivity: Install MongoDB and MongoDB Compass (or the mongo Docker container plus Compass pointed at it), connect successfully, create a database and a collection, and insert one document containing at least 3 BSON types (ObjectId, Date, nested object).
slots.deliverable: A running MongoDB instance visible in Compass with one collection containing a document that uses 3 distinct BSON types.

lessons.title: Embedding vs. Referencing: Schema Design Patterns
Data Modeling for Real-World MongoDB Applications

slots.practicalActivity: Model the same small e-commerce domain (customers, orders, products) two ways in mongosh: once with embedding (orders embed their line items) and once with referencing (line items reference a separate products collection), then run CRUD operations against both and compare query complexity.
slots.deliverable: Two working mongosh scripts (embedded version and referenced version) with CRUD operations run against each, plus a short note on which fit the access pattern better.

slots.practicalActivity: Data-modeling lab: design and build a MongoDB schema for a realistic small app (e.g., a blog with posts/comments/authors), justifying each embedding vs. referencing decision, and populate it with mongosh inserts.
slots.deliverable: A working MongoDB collection set for the chosen app plus a short design doc justifying each modeling decision.

lessons.title: The MongoDB Query Language: Filters & Projections

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 MongoDB queries against your lab data using filters and projections (e.g., comparison and logical operators, $in, field inclusion/exclusion), then build a 3-stage aggregation pipeline ($match, $group, $sort) answering a real question about the data.
slots.deliverable: 5 working filter/projection queries plus one 3-stage aggregation pipeline with its result set.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the aggregation pipeline with a $lookup joining two collections, a $group computing a per-category total, and a $facet returning two different breakdowns in one query; then create a compound index supporting your most common query and confirm it's used.
slots.deliverable: The extended aggregation pipeline's output plus an explain() excerpt showing the new compound index being used.

lessons.title: Text Search & Geospatial Queries in MongoDB

slots.practicalActivity: Create a text index and run a $text search query against one collection; create a 2dsphere index and run a geospatial $near query against location data; then run .explain('executionStats') on your busiest query and record the winning plan's index usage and scanned-vs-returned ratio.
slots.deliverable: The text-search and geospatial query results plus an explain('executionStats') output annotated with scanned-vs-returned counts.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable authentication on your MongoDB instance, create an admin user and two restricted users, create a custom role granting read-only access to one database, and assign it to one of the restricted users, confirming with db.getUser().
slots.deliverable: The createUser/createRole scripts plus db.getUser() output confirming each account's real privileges.

lessons.title: Encryption at Rest & in Transit in MongoDB

slots.practicalActivity: Configure TLS for client connections (or document the production configuration if your lab can't terminate TLS) and enable field-level or at-rest encryption for one collection; separately enable MongoDB's auditing feature and review captured events for a few operations.
slots.deliverable: Configuration excerpts for encryption and auditing plus a sample of captured audit-log entries.

slots.practicalActivity: Take a full backup with mongodump, restore it into a differently-named database with mongorestore to confirm it's valid, then run mongostat against your instance for 30 seconds while generating load and note what each column reports.
slots.deliverable: The mongodump/mongorestore commands with a verification query on the restored database, plus an annotated mongostat sample.

lessons.title: Sharding Fundamentals & Choosing a Shard Key

slots.practicalActivity: Stand up a 3-node MongoDB replica set with mongosh's rs.initiate(), confirm with rs.status() that one primary and two secondaries are healthy, kill the primary's container to confirm an automatic election promotes a new primary, then design a shard key for a sample collection, explicitly evaluating its cardinality and whether it's monotonic.
slots.deliverable: rs.status() output before and after the simulated primary failure, plus a written shard-key justification covering cardinality and monotonicity.

lessons.title: MongoDB Atlas: Managed MongoDB in the Cloud
Scaling Strategies & Capacity Planning in MongoDB

slots.practicalActivity: Stand up a minimal sharded cluster (config servers, 2 shards, mongos) with sh.shardCollection() using the shard key you designed, and confirm data distributes across both shards with sh.status(); then provision a free-tier MongoDB Atlas cluster and connect to it from mongosh or Compass.
slots.deliverable: The sh.shardCollection() command and sh.status() output showing chunks on both shards, plus proof of a successful connection to your Atlas cluster.

slots.practicalActivity: Scaling lab: migrate a sample collection from your local instance into your Atlas cluster with mongoexport/mongoimport, and document a capacity-planning estimate (storage + throughput) for 10x the current data volume.
slots.deliverable: A working Atlas cluster containing the migrated collection plus a one-page capacity-planning estimate for 10x growth.

lessons.title: Azure Cosmos DB Overview & the Multi-Model Engine
Cosmos DB APIs: Core (SQL), MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin & Table

slots.practicalActivity: Compare the Cosmos DB Core (SQL) API against the Cosmos DB for MongoDB API by writing a one-page decision memo: for a document-shaped workload already using MongoDB drivers, when would you keep the MongoDB API vs. migrate to Core (SQL) API?
slots.deliverable: A one-page Cosmos DB API decision memo with a concrete recommendation and its reasoning.

lessons.title: Provisioning a Cosmos DB Account & Container
Partitioning in Cosmos DB: Choosing a Partition Key

slots.practicalActivity: Provision an Azure Cosmos DB account (free tier) with a Core (SQL) API database and container, choosing and justifying a partition key for a sample workload (e.g., tenantId or customerId), and insert items via the Data Explorer or SDK confirming they land in the right logical partitions.
slots.deliverable: A running Cosmos DB container with a justified partition key and inserted sample items visible in Data Explorer.

lessons.title: Data Modeling for Cosmos DB's Core API

slots.practicalActivity: Model the same small app from your MongoDB lab for Cosmos DB's Core API (denormalizing per the partition key decision), then provision throughput as both manual RU/s and autoscale on two test containers and compare cost/behavior under a short burst of writes.
slots.deliverable: The Cosmos DB Core API data model for the app plus a short comparison of manual vs. autoscale RU behavior under burst load.

lessons.title: The Cosmos DB SQL Query Language
Stored Procedures, Triggers & UDFs in Cosmos DB

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 Cosmos DB SQL API queries against your container (filtering, projection, ORDER BY, a JOIN-like array unwind), write and register one stored procedure that performs a multi-item transactional update within a single partition, then enable the change feed and write a small script (Python or Node) that reads new/updated items from it in real time.
slots.deliverable: 5 working Cosmos DB SQL queries, a registered stored procedure, and the change-feed consumer script's output showing captured changes.

lessons.title: Connecting Applications with the Cosmos DB SDK
Cosmos DB for MongoDB & Cassandra Workloads

slots.practicalActivity: Customize the container's indexing policy to exclude one rarely-queried path and confirm the change with a getIndexingPolicy check; then connect to the container from the official SDK (Python, .NET, or JS) performing a create, a point read, and a cross-partition query, and repeat the same access pattern via the Cosmos DB for MongoDB API.
slots.deliverable: The modified indexing policy JSON, a working SDK script performing create/read/query, and a comparison note on the MongoDB-API equivalent.

slots.practicalActivity: Application integration lab: build a small end-to-end demo that writes an item through the Core (SQL) API SDK and confirms it's visible both via a SQL query and via the change feed consumer from the previous slot.
slots.deliverable: A working demo script plus proof the same item is visible through both the SQL query path and the change feed.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable a second write region on your Cosmos DB account (or document the steps if your subscription can't add a region), then run the same write-then-immediate-read test under Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session, and Eventual consistency levels and record the observed read result for each.
slots.deliverable: A table recording what each consistency level returned for the same write-then-read test.

lessons.title: Autoscale vs. Manual Throughput & Cost Optimization

slots.practicalActivity: Configure a last-writer-wins conflict resolution policy on a multi-region container and simulate a conflicting write from two regions to observe the resolution; then switch one container from manual throughput to autoscale and compare the billed RU/s under a spiky workload.
slots.deliverable: Evidence of the conflict resolution outcome plus a before/after cost/throughput comparison for manual vs. autoscale.

lessons.title: Designing for High Availability in Cosmos DB

slots.practicalActivity: Trigger an on-demand backup or confirm Cosmos DB's continuous backup is enabled on your account, then restore a container to a prior point in time into a new container and verify its item count matches the pre-restore state; document a high-availability design (regions + failover priority) for a real workload.
slots.deliverable: Proof of a successful point-in-time restore (item-count match) plus a one-page HA design document.

lessons.title: Cosmos DB Security: Keys, RBAC & Network Isolation
Private Endpoints & Firewall Rules for Cosmos DB

slots.practicalActivity: Rotate your Cosmos DB account's primary key and update your client to use the secondary key with zero downtime; then configure a private endpoint (or a firewall IP rule if private endpoints aren't available in your subscription) and confirm access is blocked from an unauthorized network.
slots.deliverable: Evidence of the successful key rotation plus a failed-then-allowed connection test proving the network restriction works.

lessons.title: Monitoring Cosmos DB with Azure Monitor

slots.practicalActivity: Set up an Azure Monitor metric alert on your Cosmos DB account for 429 (throttling) responses, then deliberately overload a low-RU container until you trigger real 429s, and use Azure Monitor metrics to diagnose which operation and partition caused the throttling.
slots.deliverable: The alert configuration plus a captured 429 event with its root-cause diagnosis from Azure Monitor metrics.

lessons.title: Migrating Relational Data into Cosmos DB

slots.practicalActivity: Score your Cosmos DB container design against 4 Well-Architected pillars (cost, performance, reliability, security) in a short checklist, then migrate one table from your relational lab (e.g., AdventureWorks's Person table) into Cosmos DB, documenting the schema transformation.
slots.deliverable: A completed Well-Architected scoring checklist plus a working Cosmos DB container holding the migrated relational table's data.

lessons.title: Why Graph Databases? Nodes, Relationships & Properties

slots.practicalActivity: Install Neo4j (Desktop or Docker) and open Neo4j Browser, then hand-model a small real domain (e.g., actors/movies or employees/departments) as nodes and relationships with properties, and create it directly with Cypher CREATE statements.
slots.deliverable: A running Neo4j instance with your hand-modeled graph visible in Neo4j Browser.

lessons.title: Importing Data into Neo4j (CSV, LOAD CSV)
Modeling Relational Data as a Graph

slots.practicalActivity: Import a real relational dataset (e.g., a CSV export of AdventureWorks's Person/SalesOrderHeader) into Neo4j using LOAD CSV, modeling foreign-key relationships as graph relationships, and apply graph data-modeling principles (specific relationship types, denormalized properties where it helps traversal) to the result.
slots.deliverable: A populated Neo4j graph built from the imported CSV with foreign keys expressed as real relationships, plus a short modeling-decisions note.

slots.practicalActivity: Modeling lab: given a normalized relational schema with at least 4 tables and 3 relationships, convert it into a graph model and load it into Neo4j with LOAD CSV, documenting which relational joins became graph traversals.
slots.deliverable: A loaded Neo4j graph for the 4-table schema plus a mapping table of relational joins to graph relationships.

lessons.title: Cypher Query Language Basics: MATCH & RETURN

slots.practicalActivity: Write 5 Cypher queries against your graph using MATCH/RETURN, then extend 3 of them with WHERE filters, ORDER BY, and an aggregating RETURN (count(), collect()).
slots.deliverable: 5 working Cypher MATCH/RETURN queries, with 3 extended to include filtering, sorting, and aggregation.

slots.practicalActivity: Write Cypher statements to CREATE 3 new nodes and 2 new relationships, then update an existing node's property with SET and delete one relationship with DELETE; separately write a variable-length path query (e.g., [:KNOWS*1..3]) finding all nodes within 3 hops of a given node.
slots.deliverable: The CREATE/SET/DELETE Cypher statements plus the variable-length path query's result set.

lessons.title: Query Tuning & the Cypher Query Planner

slots.practicalActivity: Write one Cypher query using a subquery (CALL {...}) to compute a per-group aggregate alongside detail rows, then run PROFILE on your most complex query to read the Cypher query planner's operator tree and identify the most expensive operator.
slots.deliverable: The subquery-based Cypher query's output plus a PROFILE output annotated with the most expensive operator identified.

lessons.title: The Neo4j Graph Data Science Library

slots.practicalActivity: Install the Neo4j Graph Data Science library (or confirm it's available in your Neo4j Desktop/Docker setup), project your graph into GDS, run the shortest-path (Dijkstra or A*) algorithm between two real nodes in your dataset, then run PageRank on the same projection and record the top 5 nodes by importance.
slots.deliverable: The GDS graph projection command, the shortest-path result between two named nodes, and the PageRank top-5 results.

lessons.title: Real-World Use Cases: Fraud Detection & Recommendations

slots.practicalActivity: Run a community-detection algorithm (Louvain) on your projected graph and record how many communities were found and their sizes, then run node-similarity to generate 3 real "similar to X" recommendations for a chosen node.
slots.deliverable: The Louvain community-detection output (community count and sizes) plus the node-similarity results for 3 recommendations.

slots.practicalActivity: Graph data science capstone lab: write a short memo on how the PageRank, community-detection, and node-similarity results you just produced could detect fraud or power a recommendation feature for a real business, citing your own actual output as evidence.
slots.deliverable: A one-page fraud-detection-or-recommendation memo grounded in your own GDS results from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable Neo4j's native authentication, create a role scoped to read-only access on one database/graph, and assign it to a new user, confirming with SHOW ROLES/SHOW USERS; then take a full backup with neo4j-admin backup/dump and restore it into a fresh instance.
slots.deliverable: The role/user creation commands with SHOW ROLES/SHOW USERS confirmation, plus proof the backup restored successfully.

lessons.title: Causal Clustering & High Availability in Neo4j

slots.practicalActivity: Document the architecture of a causal cluster (core servers + read replicas) for your dataset's expected read/write load, then run PROFILE on 2 slow Cypher queries and apply an index (CREATE INDEX) or query rewrite to improve each.
slots.deliverable: A causal-cluster sizing plan plus before/after PROFILE output for the 2 tuned queries.

lessons.title: Neo4j Aura: Managed Neo4j in the Cloud

slots.practicalActivity: Provision a free-tier Neo4j Aura instance, migrate your lab graph into it via neo4j-admin or Aura's import tool, and set up a basic monitoring check (query latency or node/relationship counts) you'd run regularly in production.
slots.deliverable: A populated Neo4j Aura instance holding the migrated graph plus a documented monitoring check.

lessons.title: Project: Choosing the Right Model for a Real Business Problem

slots.practicalActivity: Given a realistic business problem (e.g., an e-commerce platform needing product catalogs, session data, and a recommendation graph), decide which parts belong in MongoDB, Cosmos DB, and Neo4j and justify each choice in writing.
slots.deliverable: A written model-selection justification mapping each part of the business problem to MongoDB, Cosmos DB, or Neo4j.

lessons.title: Project: Connecting MongoDB, Cosmos DB & Neo4j in One Architecture

slots.practicalActivity: Build a minimal working slice of each of the 3 platforms for the business problem from the previous slot, and connect them with one small script that reads from MongoDB, Cosmos DB, and Neo4j in a single run.
slots.deliverable: A working script that successfully queries all three platforms in one run, plus the 3 minimal data slices it reads from.

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own answers to 8 realistic NoSQL/graph-database interview questions covering CAP trade-offs, sharding/partitioning pitfalls, and when graph beats relational, then do a timed mock interview answering 3 of them aloud without notes.
slots.deliverable: A written Q&A document for 8 interview questions plus notes from the timed mock-interview run.

lessons.title: Course Wrap-Up: Where NoSQL Fits in Your DBA Career

slots.practicalActivity: Reflect in writing on which of the three platforms (MongoDB, Cosmos DB, Neo4j) you'd reach for first on your next real project and why, and identify one gap in your knowledge you'd close before using it in production.
slots.deliverable: A one-page reflection naming a preferred platform, the reasoning, and one concrete follow-up learning goal.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone build-out, part 1: extend the 3-platform mini-architecture from the project slots with one more realistic requirement (a MongoDB aggregation report, a Cosmos DB change-feed consumer, or a Neo4j recommendation query feeding back into the app).
slots.deliverable: The extended 3-platform mini-architecture with the new requirement implemented and demonstrably working.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone build-out, part 2: write a one-page architecture diagram and an operations runbook a teammate could follow to run, monitor, and recover the finished 3-platform mini-architecture.
slots.deliverable: A one-page architecture diagram plus an operations runbook covering running, monitoring, and recovering the system.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can model, query, secure, scale, and operate real workloads on MongoDB, Azure Cosmos DB, and Neo4j, and can justify which non-relational model fits a given business problem.
